title: Exploring the thermoelectric and electronic transport properties of Janus ISbTe and IAsSe: a DFT-NEGF study
content: Thermoelectric materials capable of converting heat into electricity are essential for sustainable energy technologies. In this work, we investigate the electronic structure, thermoelectric properties and electronic transport characteristics of two-dimensional (2D) Janus ISbTe and IAsSe materials using density functional theory (DFT), Boltzmann transport theory, and non-equilibrium Green's function (NEGF). The calculated band structures reveal that ISbTe and IAsSe have indirect band gaps with the values of 1.16 eV and 1.31 eV, respectively. The broken inversion symmetry of these Janus materials gives rise to favourable electronic transport characteristics. The obtained Seebeck coefficients of ISbTe and IAsSe are −247 µV K−1 and −800 µV K−1, respectively. Both materials also exhibit high electrical conductivity per relaxation time. The calculated dimensionless figure of merit (ZT) reveals that ISbTe exhibits a higher ZT than IAsSe over the studied temperature range. The calculated electronic transport properties from DFT-NEGF calculations of ISbTe and IAsSe demonstrate that an applied temperature gradient across a two-probe device generates thermoelectric current in both materials. Our investigation illustrates that Janus ISbTe and IAsSe are promising candidates for applications in nanoscale thermoelectric energy conversion, waste heat recovery, and thermal-gradient-driven electronic devices.
